title: Observability Contracts and Dependency SLO Onboarding Handbook
author: Iris Montgomery
content:
Summary
-------
This handbook defines the observability contract that every service on Redwood’s platform must satisfy before receiving production traffic. The contract focuses on dependency-level SLIs/SLOs, telemetry shape and cardinality limits, baseline dashboards, alerting thresholds, and automated verification steps. The goal is to reduce mean time to detect and resolve cross-service reliability issues and to ensure consistent telemetry that enables cost-aware routing, predictive batching, and incident triage.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all new and migrated services that register in the platform service registry.
- Covers both HTTP/gRPC services and async workers that call platform runtimes (e.g., inference runtime, KV cache).
- Does NOT replace per-team product SLAs; rather it provides a baseline operational surface for platform-level tooling and routing.

Definitions
-----------
- Observability contract: A minimal, machine-verifiable set of telemetry, dashboards, and alerting that a service must satisfy.
- Dependency SLI: Metric measuring the surface area where a downstream depends on an upstream (e.g., p95 latency to model-serving endpoint).
- SLO: Objective for an SLI (expressed with target and window, e.g., 99.9% success over 30d).
- Telemetry contract: Specification for naming conventions, labels/tags, event volumes, and exemplar tracing.

Why this matters
----------------
- Standardized signals accelerate incident triage across teams.
- Consistent dependency SLIs enable platform-wide routing policies (fallbacks, hybrid burst).
- Controlling telemetry shape reduces ingest costs and avoids high-cardinality explosions in dashboards.

Observability Contract — Required Items
--------------------------------------
1) Telemetry and Traces
   - Request-level spans for every external dependency call with the following tags: service.name, env, tenant_id (when applicable), upstream_dependency, request_type, route, model_variant (if calling runtime).
   - Traces should propagate a single trace_id and include at least one span-level error marker and an error.message when failures occur.
   - Maximum cardinality: no more than 5 custom tag values per request for platform-level tags (platform will enforce sampled dimensions).

2) Metrics (Prometheus/OTel) — required metrics and labels
   - dependency_request_total{upstream="<service>", result="success|error|timeout|cancelled", env="prod|staging"}
   - dependency_request_duration_seconds_bucket (histogram) labeled with upstream and route
   - dependency_request_errors_total with an error_code label (HTTP code or internal error code)
   - local_processing_duration_seconds for the calling service (histogram)
   - Labels required on all metrics: service, team, env, shard (optional)

3) SLIs/SLOs (template)
   - Upstream success SLI: ratio of dependency_request_total{result="success"} to total over 30d.
   - Upstream latency SLI: p95 of dependency_request_duration_seconds over 7d with SLO 99th percentile of calls <= target_ms.
   - Default platform SLOs (can be tightened by owners):
     * Success rate: 99.5% over 30d for internal infra dependencies
     * Latency: p95 <= 300ms over 7d for model-serving dependencies (adjust by model size)
   - Teams can request exceptions via eng-platform review if the dependency is best-effort or has known tail-latency characteristics.

4) Dashboards (baseline)
   - A per-service "Dependency Overview" dashboard with panels:
     1. Dependency success rate (30d)
     2. Latency histogram and heatmap (p50/p95/p99)
     3. Error breakdown by error_code
     4. Trace sampling view (recent errors) linked to spans
     5. Request volume and cardinality signals
   - Dashboard template is available at: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/dependency-dashboard-template (use this as starting point).

5) Alerts — required alert set
   - dependency-success-rate-breach: fires when success rate < SLO threshold over a sliding 1h and 24h window.
   - dependency-latency-tail: fires when p99 latency > configured threshold for 10m.
   - dependency-error-spike: fires when error rate increases by >3x baseline in 5m.
   - Alert routing: all three map to the owning team’s primary oncall; platform-runbook annotations must be attached automatically by the alerting system.

Onboarding Checklist (Step-by-step)
-----------------------------------
1) Pre-registration (developer):
   - Fill the Service Registration form in the platform registry with primary owner, team, dependency list, and expected QPS.
   - Attach the intended SLO targets for each dependency.
2) Instrumentation (developer):
   - Implement required metrics and tracing as listed above.
   - Add auto-instrumentation for HTTP/gRPC if available; otherwise implement client wrappers that emit the mandated labels.
3) Automated verification (CI):
   - Add a CI job that runs the observability contract linter (see sample below). The job must run on PRs that change service code.
   - Contract linter checks: presence of metric names, required labels, trace propagation headers, and example span present in integration test traces.
4) Dashboard & Alerts (platform + developer):
   - Apply the dashboard template and set SLO thresholds.
   - Configure alerts and verify routing to oncall using the test alert endpoint.
5) Gating & Release (platform):
   - The platform gating job will query the service’s sandbox telemetry for 48h. If all checks pass, the service receives the production traffic flag.

Automated verification: sample CI snippet
----------------------------------------
- Sample Makefile target:
  * verify-observability-contract:
    - run: observability-linter --metrics "dependency_request_total,dependency_request_duration_seconds_bucket" --tracing-required
    - run: curl -f https://platform.tools.redwood/check-sandbox?service=$SERVICE_NAME

Telemetry Cost & Cardinality Guidelines
--------------------------------------
- Per-service ingest cap (non-exempt): 50M metric samples/month. Request increases via platform approval.
- High-cardinality labels: avoid free-form IDs (use hashed buckets or sampling). If a label has >100 unique values/day at normal traffic, mark it as high-cardinality and route to sampled telemetry only.

Ownership and Escalation
------------------------
- Service owner: responsible for instrumentation, dashboards, and initial alert tuning.
- Platform SRE: responsible for verifying telemetry shape and enforcing ingest caps.
- Escalation path: oncall -> team lead -> platform SRE -> CTO (if incident >= Sev1 lasting >3h).

Verification & Rollback Criteria
-------------------------------
- Pass criteria in sandbox: all required metrics present, at least 99.9% trace propagation on sampled requests, dashboard panels render without missing series.
- Rollback if production onboarding introduces >2x baseline error rate or latency increase leading to downstream SLO breaches. Rollback steps are in the runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/cold-start-warmup-orchestration-runbook-2026.

Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them
-------------------------------------
- Too many dynamic labels: use coarse-grained buckets (e.g., model_variant=large|small|quantized) instead of model config hash.
- Uninstrumented background retries: ensure retry loops emit a separate metric to avoid double-counting.
- High trace sampling with heavy payloads: sample at 1% for high-volume requests and enable full sampling for error traces.

Roadmap Items (next 12 months)
------------------------------
- Q2 2025: Enforce ingest caps with automated throttling and alerting for spikes.
- Q3 2025: Add platform-backed telemetry schema registry and automated migration tooling.
- Q4 2025: Build a dependency SLO catalog view in the Console to surface cross-team SLO impacts.

Appendix: Useful links and snippets
----------------------------------
- Observability linter repo: git@internal:redwood/observability-linter
- Dashboard template: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/dependency-dashboard-template
- Contract checklist CLI: tools/contract-checker --service $SERVICE_NAME --env sandbox

Contact and ownership
---------------------
Document owner: eng-platform (observability). For questions or exceptions, file an RFC in the platform-team channel (#eng-platform-observability) or email eng-platform@redwood.ai.
